newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan buys 315,000 T U.S., Australian wheat.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan buys 315,000 T U.S., Australian wheat.

text.p: Pakistan has bought 180,000 tonnes of Australian wheat and 135,000 of U.S. soft white wheat at $150 to $155 a tonne, a U.S. official said on Wednesday.
The agriculture attache at the U.S. embassy said the Ministry of Food and Agriculture had bought four 45,000-tonne cargoes of Australian wheat at $155 a tonne.
It had also bought three 45,000-tonne cargoes of U.S. wheat at $150 to $151 a tonne, he said.

The ministry, which had issued side-by-side tenders for 315,000 tonnes of Australian or U.S. wheat, opened the bids on Sunday, but did not take an immediate decision. "We accepted the lowest bids," an official at the ministry said.
The U.S. agriculture attache said he expected Pakistan to tender again for a similar quantity around February 9.
At the last tender on December 1, Pakistan bought 225,000 tonnes of Australian wheat from Cargill at about $152 per tonne for December 11-31 shipment.

Officials say Pakistan expects to buy a total of 2.3 million tonnes of wheat in 1996/97 (July-June). It had initially hoped to hold imports to 1.8 million tonnes, but revised its import target in December after domestic production fell to 17 million tonnes from 17.57 million tonnes in 1995/96.
